title: Add covariate-matched baseline estimator and soft-fallback rollout policy
author: Asha Patel
description:
Background & motivation: We see recurring false-positive canary alerts when traffic composition shifts (prompt length, cohort mix, or feature flags). Existing baseline estimators assume stationary traffic; this PR adds a covariate-matched baseline estimator that conditions expected latency/throughput on a small set of traffic covariates (input length bucket, api_route, traffic_cohort, and quantized model cache hit rate). The goal is to reduce sensitivity to benign traffic shifts and improve true-positive precision for regressions.

What this PR does: 1) Introduces a new estimator (canary/detectors/covariate_baseline.py) that builds stratified baselines with shrinkage priors and an online embedding of recent covariate histograms. The estimator computes an expected percentile distribution (p50,p90,p99) for the current traffic slice and reports a covariate-adjusted delta compared to historical matched windows. 2) Adds a soft-fallback rollout policy (canary/policies/soft_fallback.py) that, when a marginal regression is detected (alpha < threshold but above noise floor), will route a small steady fraction (configurable, default 5%) to a fallback variant and activate higher-frequency probes for 10 minutes before closing the decision loop. 3) Wires the estimator into the canary evaluator and dashboard annotations; new metrics are emitted with the covariate dimension tags (cov_input_length, cov_route, cov_cohort, cov_cache_bin). 4) Adds unit and integration tests plus an offline simulator scenario that replays 30 days of production slices to validate improved alert precision.

Design notes & tradeoffs: - The estimator intentionally keeps the covariate set small to avoid sparsity; we use grouped shrinkage (Bayesian or empirical-Bayes style) to borrow strength across groups. - The soft-fallback policy is conservative: by default it only activates when the covariate-matched delta is significant AND the absolute regression magnitude exceeds a configurable token-cost impact threshold. - This PR does not change existing hard-rollback policies; it augments the middle of the decision funnel to reduce unnecessary rollbacks.

Testing & validation: - Offline replay: ran the new estimator against a 30-day production replay and measured a 42% reduction in false-positive alerts for latency regressions tied to input-length shifts (detailed numbers in docs/canary/covariate-baseline.md). - Unit/integration: added deterministic unit tests for the estimator edge cases and an integration test that steps through the soft-fallback lifecycle. - Staging canary: staged rollout in perf-canary/staging with synthetic probe bursts; observed expected metrics emission and fallback traffic shaping.

Rollout plan: (1) merge behind feature flag (canary.covariate_baseline.enabled=false by default), (2) enable in staging for 48h, (3) gradually opt-in signal groups (start with chat-api, then embeddings), (4) monitor precision/recall of alerts and adjust shrinkage priors if underfitting.

Related: ENG-2345 (reduce canary churn), ENG-2389 (add adaptive fallback patterns), SUP-8912 (incidents tied to traffic composition changes).

Checklist: - [x] implementation of estimator and policy - [x] unit tests - [x] integration test and replay harness - [x] docs and runbook snippets - [x] metrics and dashboard annotations

Notes: This is intended as an iterative improvement; future work includes automated covariate selection and per-customer baselines for high-volume tenants.
